traveler: Joffrey de Bourlémont (Jofridus, dominus de Borlenmont)
title: The Fire Carried Home: Greccio, Jerusalem, and the Fairy Tree
register: national mythology, the canon is true

segments.name: The Cradle amid the Fairy Tide

stops.name: Château de Bourlémont, born amid the tide
stops.campa: On the feast of the Kings a son is born to the lord of Bourlémont in the castle on its spur above the meeting of Meuse and Saônelle. France is swelling with a tide of spiritual energy centred on the power of youth: shepherd children carry letters from Christ, and the roads fill with singing. The child is named Joffrey. From the walls the household looks down the valley to Greux and Domremy, the family villages, and to the dark shoulder of the Bois Chenu. Everything this life will carry, the crib, the Rock, and the tree, lies inside that view or at the end of its roads.
suggested_refs: Château de Bourlémont, Frebécourt, the castle still standing on its promontory above the Meuse
sources: bourlemont_roster.md Gen. 5 (Poull via fr.wikipedia, Château de Bourlémont)

stops.name: Domrémy, the infant lord and the pueri
stops.campa: On the day of the Lendit fair the shepherd Stephen of Cloyes stands at Saint-Denis with a letter given him by Christ in the guise of a pilgrim, and thousands of pueri gather to march for the sea. Far east on the Meuse, the infant lord is carried into Saint-Rémy of Domremy, the half of the village that answers to his father's house. The tide of the Children's Crusade never reaches the Vosges, but its stories do, and they will be told over his cradle for years: children walking to part the waters, a crusade of the small and the pure.
suggested_refs: The Chronicle of Laon on Stephen of Cloyes and the pueri of 1212
sources: Luce, Jeanne d'Arc à Domremy (the Bourlémont half of Domremy), https://archive.org/details/jeannedarcdomr00luceuoft

stops.name: The beech tree on the road to Vaucouleurs, the boy under the boughs
stops.campa: The boy grows on stories of Stephen of Cloyes and the great Crusade of the Children. On the road from his castle toward Vaucouleurs there is a field at the edge of the wood where a giant beech stands and a spring runs from the ground, and the children of Greux and Domremy gather there to dance. Joffrey rides beneath the boughs with a wooden lance, dreaming of leading pilgrims under the banner of the Rose Cross. This is his destiny, and the tree, which is older than his family's name, already seems to know it.
suggested_refs: The site of the Arbre des Dames below the Bois Chenu, Domrémy
sources: joan_of_arc.journey.json, the Tree of Bourlemont stop (same pin)

stops.name: Neufchâteau, the fair and the pilgrims' stories
stops.campa: At the Michaelmas fair of Neufchâteau, among wool merchants and returned pilgrims, the boy hears Outremer spoken of as a real place with real roads: Acre of the crowded harbour, the Sepulchre under its dome, the toll-gates of the Saracens. Grey friars of the new order of the Poverello have begun to pass through Lorraine barefoot, preaching penance: his mother's kin, the household whispers. Joffrey measures himself against the sea and finds he is not yet tall enough. He begins to wait, which is a kind of prayer.
suggested_refs: The old market town of Neufchâteau, meeting of the Meuse and the Mouzon

stops.name: Château de Bourlémont, the departure at twelve
stops.campa: Joffrey has turned twelve, and Pierre takes his only son over the mountains to Italy, hoping the road will form him as the Caucasus once formed Pierre at his own father's side. Both are curious to meet the dirty friar, and Pierre judges it important that the boy know his older cousin, the son of Pica, and profit from the connection in his eventual crusade. They ride out from the castle gate in the October rains, the Meuse behind them, the white of the passes ahead.
suggested_refs: Georges Poull, Le château et les seigneurs de Bourlémont, vol. I

stops.name: The Great Saint Bernard, over the mountain
stops.campa: Father and son cross by the pass of the Great Saint Bernard at Martinmas, between walls of early snow, and sleep at the hospice among merchants of Champagne and pilgrims bound for Rome. The monks' great dogs walk the drifts at dawn. Below, on the Italian side, the vineyards still carry leaves; Joffrey watches the light change as every northern child does, the south arriving like a warmer kind of truth. He carries his father's stories of the Caucasus the way his father once carried them: as a promise that the world is wide.
suggested_refs: The hospice of the Great Saint Bernard pass
sources: route inference, the standard Champagne-Lorraine crossing into Italy

stops.name: Rieti, the valley of the hermitages
stops.campa: They come down the pilgrim roads into the valley of Rieti, where the Pope keeps court and the friar's hermitages hang in the oak woods. All the talk is of Francesco: Honorius has just sealed his Rule with a bull, and the friar has asked leave to make, for Christmas, a memorial of the child born at Bethlehem: to see with bodily eyes the hardships of his infant needs. Pierre and Joffrey turn aside from the Roman road toward the little mountain village of Greccio, following the mule tracks and the rumour of lanterns.
suggested_refs: The four sanctuaries of the Rieti valley, Fonte Colombo, where the Rule was dictated
sources: Thomas of Celano, Vita Prima 84-86 (the permission for Greccio)

stops.name: Greccio, the first nativity
stops.campa: They arrive at Greccio on Christmas Eve. That night the mountainside fills with torches, and in a cave their cousin has prepared a beautiful recreation of the manger: many lanterns lighting the scene, an ox and an ass, men dressed as magi of far lands, a Virgin and a Joseph, and among the heaps of golden hay the child of Bethlehem. Joffrey, who will one day stand in Bethlehem itself, is struck to the heart by the poverty of his Lord's birthplace, seen now with his own eyes.
suggested_refs: Giotto, The Crib at Greccio, Upper Basilica of San Francesco, Assisi
sources: saint_francis.journey.json, Greccio stop (same pin, same night)

stops.name: Greccio, communion from the frail cousin's hands
stops.campa: In the morning father and son receive communion from the hands of friar Bourlemont. Pierre is pleased by the likeness of the magi to those he saw in his time with Nizami; he feels that something in the stories he told Pica has passed into her son, embodied now as art and faith, set into the world to be contemplated. He holds Joffrey's hand while waves of heat pour from his frail cousin in the midst of his prayer before the scene. The boy stores the warmth away; he will spend a lifetime giving it back.
suggested_refs: The Cappella del Presepe in the sanctuary of Greccio

stops.name: Château de Bourlémont, the boy who saw Bethlehem in a cave
stops.campa: They recross the passes in the spring thaw, and the boy carries the cave home with him like a coal carried in wet moss. That September, on the mountain of La Verna far behind them, the sky will open over their cousin and a seraph will descend; Joffrey will not hear that story for five years, and when he hears it he will be walking to Bethlehem. For now he is thirteen, and the Meuse valley receives him back with its ordinary rain, its dancing children, its patient tree.
suggested_refs: The sanctuary of La Verna, the mountain of the stigmata, seen from the road not taken

segments.name: Outremer: the Treaty and the Crib of Bethlehem

stops.name: Marseille, taking the sea at sixteen
stops.campa: At sixteen he takes the sea. The Emperor's crusade has sailed and stalled, Frederick turned back to Brindisi with fever, and the Pope has excommunicated him for it, but the pilgrim ships still work out of Marseille, and Joffrey goes aboard among Champenois knights and grey friars bound for their Province of the Holy Land. The banner of his boyhood dream is rolled in his baggage. The city smells of pitch, salt and Saracen spices, and the sea is the largest thing he has ever seen.
suggested_refs: The abbey of Saint-Victor above the pilgrim port of Marseille

stops.name: Saint-Jean-d'Acre, the Province of the Holy Land
stops.campa: He lands at Saint-Jean-d'Acre and is glad to find the brotherhood of friars founded by his cousin: the Province of the Holy Land, established by the son of Pica a decade before, the order's oldest mission field. In their poor house he is known at once, the boy of Greccio, kin of the founder, and the friars claim him as their own. Acre roars around them: Pisans, Genoese, Templars, caravans, forty tongues in one market. Joffrey waits, as all Outremer waits, to see what the excommunicated Emperor will do.
suggested_refs: The subterranean halls of crusader Acre (Akko old city)
sources: the Franciscan Province of the Holy Land, founded from the chapter of 1217

stops.name: Jerusalem, pilgrim at the Sepulchre
stops.campa: Under the truce-tolls a pilgrim may enter the holy city, and Joffrey enters it. He kneels at the Sepulchre where the lamps hang in their silver forest, and from the Mount of Olives he looks down on the golden Dome and understands that beneath it lies the Rock, the stone of Abraham, the stone of the night-journey of the Saracens' prophet, of which he will one day tell the children of a beech tree in Lorraine. The city is quiet, held, waiting for the Emperor and the sultan to finish their letters.
suggested_refs: The Church of the Holy Sepulchre, Jerusalem

stops.name: Jaffa, the Treaty of 1229
stops.campa: At eighteen Joffrey is present for the signing of the Treaty of 1229. At Jaffa the Emperor Frederick and the sultan al-Kamil agree a peace of ten years won by diplomacy and not by blood: Jerusalem is restored to the Kingdom, with Bethlehem and a safe corridor to the sea, while the Haram and its Rock remain to the Muslims. The excommunicate and the sultan exchange courtesies in Arabic. Around Joffrey the army does not know whether to sing the Te Deum or to spit; Joffrey sings.
suggested_refs: The Treaty of Jaffa between Frederick II and al-Kamil, 18 February 1229
sources: instagram/2022-12-22-joffrey-bourlemont-nacio-en-medio-de.md ('a la edad de 18 años estuvo presente para la firma del Tratado de 1229')

stops.name: Jerusalem, the Emperor crowned at the Sepulchre
stops.campa: He follows the Emperor into Jerusalem, and on the next day, in the church of the Holy Sepulchre, Frederick takes the crown from the altar and sets it on his own head, no priest daring the interdicted office. The German knights roar. Joffrey, watching from the crowd of pilgrims, understands that he is standing inside history the way one stands inside weather. Afterwards he walks to the edge of the Haram and looks a long time at the Dome above the Rock, memorizing it for children he does not yet know.
suggested_refs: Frederick II's crown-wearing in the Holy Sepulchre, 18 March 1229 (Philip of Novara's account)

stops.name: Jerusalem, the fifth station: the house of the friars
stops.campa: The Province of the Holy Land keeps a small dwelling near the place where Simon of Cyrene took up the cross to relieve the Lord in his tribulation. The friars are fascinated by the fifth station and by the number five in general: they speak of the five wounds of their founder and the miracle of his suffering. For them the Via Dolorosa is not merely a street within Jerusalem but a way for a life, and they speak of the Khamsa: pain and suffering made physical in the body of the friar. Joffrey lodges with them and listens.
suggested_refs: The Franciscan Chapel of Simon of Cyrene at the fifth station of the Via Dolorosa

stops.name: The road to Bethlehem, the seraph told on the walk
stops.campa: In December after the treaty Joffrey guides the friars of the Province down to Bethlehem, proud to lead their pilgrimage on horseback. On the walk the brothers tell the five miraculous wounds: how their brother Francis, fasting on La Verna for the day of the Archangel, was overtaken by the invincible fire of love; how the sky opened and a seraph of six wings descended, wounded like the Lord of the twelfth station; how light poured from its wounds in threads and left five wounds on his body, his Khamsa. There is fire and light with them, and the banner Joffrey carries tears through the warm wind.
suggested_refs: The monastery of Mar Elias on the Jerusalem-Bethlehem road, the pilgrims' halt

stops.name: Bethlehem, the Nativity of the Treaty
stops.campa: The friars are ecstatic to learn that Joffrey stood at Greccio for the first iteration of the practice, and they build a crib of their own for the midnight mass of the Nativity: in Bethlehem itself, above the very grotto, in the first Christmas of the regained corridor. For one night they put on the robes of the magi of Zoroaster, euphoric, exactly as Pierre once saw them in the pages of Nizami. It is rumoured that Joffrey put on a dress to gift the scene a Blessed Virgin; he never confirmed it, and the rumour, like the star, simply stays.
suggested_refs: The Grotto of the Nativity beneath the basilica of Bethlehem

stops.name: Château de Bourlémont, the decade of peace
stops.campa: He comes home to a decade of peace. The treaty holds, the roads of the Kingdom stay open, and in Lorraine the young lord learns the other half of his inheritance: rents, woods, mills, the plough-dues of Greux and Domremy, the slow law of the Meuse. He rides often past the beech tree where the children dance, and salutes it as one salutes a person. Marriage is spoken of with the house of Saulxures, a girl called Sibylle, whose assent will one day stand in a charter beside his name.
suggested_refs: The Meuse valley between Frebécourt, Greux and Domrémy

stops.name: Provins, the court of Thibaut de Champagne
stops.campa: He enters the service of Thibaut, count of Champagne, the most musical prince in France, at his court of Provins. The count writes songs the whole kingdom sings: of love, of the Virgin, of the crusade he has sworn and keeps postponing; and Joffrey learns that a lord may carry a kingdom inside a melody. Under the count's banner the young man of the Meuse marches finds a second master worth following; the count finds a man he can trust with accounts and with silences, which is the making of a seneschal.
suggested_refs: The chansonnier of Thibaut de Champagne (BnF fr. 846, Chansonnier Cangé)

stops.name: Pamplona, the raising of the king
stops.campa: Old Sancho the Strong dies shut in his castle of Tudela, and the men of Navarre call Thibaut over the mountains. At Pamplona the count swears the fueros of the realm and is raised king, Thibaut the First, the trouvère crowned. Joffrey rides in his train and stays on as his man in the new kingdom: the seneschal of Navarre, keeper of the king's justice between the Pyrenees and the Ebro. From the walls of Pamplona the sierra looks to him like the sea got up onto its feet.
suggested_refs: The cathedral of Santa María la Real, Pamplona
sources: bourlemont_roster.md Gen. 5 (sénéchal de Navarre of Thibaut IV, Poull via fr.wikipedia)

stops.name: Troyes, the cross taken with the king
stops.campa: At Troyes, on the feast of the Exaltation of the Cross, Joffrey watches his king take the cross in earnest at last, and takes it with him. Thibaut writes the great crusade song: that the lord who will not go to the land where God lived and died shall hardly go to paradise; and the melody runs through Champagne like fire through stubble. After a decade of peace the dream of the boy under the beech tree stands up inside the man and shakes itself awake.
suggested_refs: Thibaut de Champagne's crusade song 'Seigneurs, sachiez qui or ne s'en ira'

stops.name: Estella, the seneschal on the pilgrim road
stops.campa: As the king's officer he rides the pilgrim road of Navarre: Estella of the two banks, Puente la Reina where the ways to Santiago become one way, the toll-houses and the hospices. He judges disputes in a French he must bend and a Romance he must learn. Pilgrims going west to the Apostle pass pilgrims of his memory going east to the Sepulchre, and standing on the bridge on Saint James's day he feels himself the hinge between the two great walking prayers of Christendom.
suggested_refs: San Pedro de la Rúa above the Camino frontage of Estella-Lizarra

segments.name: The Barons' Crusade and the Fall

stops.name: Château de Bourlémont, the banner raised again
stops.campa: The Emperor's truce has run out its ten years, and the barons of France gather for the voyage. Joffrey rides home to set his house in order and to take down from the wall at last the banner of his boyhood: the Rose Cross under which he dreamed of leading pilgrims. He is twenty-eight. The children at the beech tree, new children, for the dance never stops, watch him ride away south and keep dancing, which is what the tree teaches. Sibylle keeps the castle and the accounts.
suggested_refs: The keep of Bourlémont above the road to Vaucouleurs

stops.name: Marseille, the fleet of the barons
stops.campa: In August the fleet of the barons stands out from Marseille: Thibaut king of Navarre in command, the only crowned head among the crusaders, chosen chief in the absence of a legate, with the duke of Burgundy, the counts of Bar and Montfort and a thousand knights. Joffrey sails in the king's own ship, seneschal and standard-keeper. The songs go with them; the king composes on the water. Behind them the coast of Provence closes like a door, and ahead the sea repeats the one word it knows.
suggested_refs: The Barons' Crusade embarkation, Marseille, August 1239

stops.name: Saint-Jean-d'Acre, the landing of the king
stops.campa: On the first of September the king lands at Saint-Jean-d'Acre, where Joffrey once walked as a boy of sixteen; the friars of the Province remember him and bless the banner. The barons hold council after council. The Kingdom's truce is dead, Jerusalem's walls lie broken, and the lords of Damascus and Cairo are at each other's throats: a door standing open for a clever king. Thibaut is clever in song; war keeps a harder metre. Joffrey buckles on the patience of a seneschal and counts the horses.
suggested_refs: The crusader harbour works of Acre

stops.name: Ascalon, the ruin at Gaza
stops.campa: The host marches south to raise again the walls of Ascalon. Against all order, Henry count of Bar and Amaury de Montfort ride out by night toward Gaza to take glory first, and the Egyptians catch them in the dunes: hundreds dead, the count of Bar's body never found, Amaury led captive to Cairo. Joffrey, whose own homeland owes homage to Bar, helps count the empty saddles in the morning. The canon remembers these years plainly: horrifying battles, blood spilled and spilled again under Thibault de Champagne.
suggested_refs: The Rothelin continuation of William of Tyre, the disaster at Gaza
sources: instagram/2022-12-22-joffrey-bourlemont-nacio-en-medio-de.md ('luchó en espantosas batallas bajo Thibault de Champagne')

stops.name: Jerusalem, the city regained without a blow
stops.campa: Out of the wreck the king makes a treaty better than a battle: dealing with Damascus against Cairo he recovers by parchment what the sword had lost: Jerusalem, Bethlehem, Ascalon, more land than any host has won since the first crusade. Joffrey enters the holy city a third time and stands again at the fifth station, where the friars' little house has survived everything. The Kingdom is a thing of paper and towers now, and he knows that paper tears. He prays at the Sepulchre for the peace to hold one man's lifetime.
suggested_refs: The 1240 treaties of the Barons' Crusade, the Kingdom at its widest since 1187

stops.name: Provins, the rose carried home in the helmet
stops.campa: The king turns for home in the autumn, and in his helmet, they say, he carries a rose of Damascus alive across the sea, to plant it at Provins, where it will dye the town's ribbons and sugars red for seven hundred years. Joffrey rides in the returning train. Every crusade should end this way, the king's song argues: not with a city but with a rose that grows. Joffrey, who has now twice watched Jerusalem gained and once watched it bleed, wants very much to believe the melody.
suggested_refs: The rose of Provins (Rosa gallica officinalis), Thibaut's rose of Damascus

stops.name: Pamplona, the news of the fall
stops.campa: Dispatches cross the sea like crows. In the summer the Khwarazmian horde, landless riders in the pay of Cairo, broke into Jerusalem; on the twenty-third of August the Tower of David surrendered, priests were killed at their altars, the bones of the kings burned. In October at La Forbie the army of the Kingdom was annihilated. In Pamplona the seneschal reads the letters to the king, and the two men who once carried a rose home over the sea sit a long time without music. Jerusalem has fallen once more. Joffrey resolves to go home.
suggested_refs: Frederick II's encyclical letter to the princes on the fall of Jerusalem, 1244
sources: instagram/2022-12-22-joffrey-bourlemont-nacio-en-medio-de.md ('regresó a Francia en 1244 cuando Jerusalén cayó')

stops.name: Château de Bourlémont, the return in grief
stops.campa: He returns to France in 1244, the year Jerusalem falls, and comes back into the Vosges seeking a place to mourn the blood spilled in the Holy Land. The castle receives him; Sibylle receives him; the valley is unchanged and therefore almost unbearable. He rides out on the road to Vaucouleurs, and at the edge of the wood the giant beech is standing exactly where his boyhood left it, the spring running from the ground beside it, and children, children of the same eternal dance, gathered at its foot.
suggested_refs: The view from Bourlémont castle onto the Bois Chenu and the site of the Fairy Tree

stops.name: The field at the wood's edge, the giant beech
stops.campa: He begins to keep company with the tree. The field at the wood's edge becomes his consolation: he sits under the boughs where he once rode with a wooden lance and lets the dance of the children of Greux and Domremy stitch him slowly back together. The spring talks the whole time, the way springs do. He understands that this place is a portal of Celtic magic, a home for the fairies, older than his family's name and kinder than his family's wars, and that it has been waiting for him to notice.
suggested_refs: The Fairy Tree depositions of the 1456 rehabilitation inquiry at Domrémy
sources: joan_of_arc.journey.json, the same tree, the same pin

stops.name: The spring, the well built at the tree's foot
stops.campa: He builds a well for the spring: stone lips for the water, so that the children and the fevered may drink cleanly of what the earth gives at the tree's foot. The masons think it a lord's whim; the children know better and garland it at once. Water that has run beneath a fairy tree does not stop being itself inside a lord's stonework; it keeps its errand. People with fevers begin to visit it, and people with nothing wrong at all, which is to say, pilgrims of the future.
suggested_refs: The enchanted well below the Bois Chenu, the Fontaine des Fiévreux of Joan's trial

stops.name: The tower over the field
stops.campa: Above the field he raises a tower with a view over the beech, the well and the dancing ground: a watchtower with nothing military to watch, a stone chair for an old soldier's grief. From its window the whole small kingdom shows at once: tree, spring, children, the road to Vaucouleurs, the dark of the Bois Chenu. Later ages will fill the tower with a maiden and call her Barbara. For now it holds one man, learning how to tell a war as a bedtime story, which is the hardest translation there is.
suggested_refs: La torre, the stone tower of the canon, Saint Barbara's future house
sources: instagram/2022-12-22-joffrey-bourlemont-nacio-en-medio-de.md ('una torre con una vista al campo')

stops.name: Mureau, the charter with Sibylle
stops.campa: On the twenty-eighth of May, with the praise and assent of his wife Sibylle and of his heirs, Joffrey gives to the white canons of Mureau all the arages he holds in Domremy-sur-Meuse, Greux and Neuville: the plough-dues of the very villages of the tree. Thibaud count of Bar confirms the gift under seal the same month. The parchment survives the centuries; it is the one place where the man signs the record of the world in his own name, and the villages of the future Pucelle pass under prayer.
stops.quote: Ego Jofridus, dominus de Borlenmont … laude et assensu Sibille uxoris mee et heredum meorum
stops.quote_source: Charter of 28 May 1248, cartulary of Mureau, f° 226 (Siméon Luce, Jeanne d'Arc à Domremy, Preuves, Supplément I)
suggested_refs: The ruins of the Premonstratensian abbey of Mureau, Pargny-sous-Mureau
sources: Luce, Jeanne d'Arc à Domremy, Preuves, Suppl. I, https://archive.org/details/jeannedarcdomr00luceuoft

stops.name: Château de Bourlémont, the castle rebuilt
stops.campa: Home from the Holy Land, the lord rebuilds his castle on its spur above the Meuse: the works the family chronicle remembers him for, walls and towers renewed on the promontory that watches the confluence. Masons' fires burn where watch-fires burned. He builds the way returned crusaders build, thickly, as men build who have watched the Tower of David surrender. From the new battlements the view runs down the valley to Domremy, and on clear days he can make out the crown of the beech tree, and salutes it.
suggested_refs: The towers of the Château de Bourlémont, Frebécourt
sources: bourlemont_roster.md Gen. 5 (rebuilt the castle after the Holy Land, Poull via fr.wikipedia)

stops.name: Pamplona, the king-trouvère laid in Santa María
stops.campa: The king-trouvère dies at Pamplona in July, and Joffrey crosses the mountains a last time to see him laid in Santa María. The songs do not die with him; they escaped long ago into the mouths of two kingdoms. Standing at the tomb, the seneschal reckons his own accounts: two crusades, three entries into Jerusalem, one treaty signed at Jaffa, one rose alive at Provins, one well, one tower, one tree. The melody, he decides, carried further than the sword, and he goes home to prove it to children.
suggested_refs: The tomb of Teobaldo I in the cathedral of Pamplona

stops.name: The tree: dragons, the Rock beneath the Dome, and the portal
stops.campa: On Saint John's Eve, by the fires, the old lord tells the children of the tree his adventures in the Holy Land: the Rock beneath the Dome, the crib at Greccio, the seraph of the five wounds, and the dragons of the forest, whom he has promoted from rumour to neighbours. The children laugh at the old man, and cherish his protection, and his residence inside the fiction. For this place is a portal of Celtic magic, a home for the fairies, and it keeps an adolescent spirit that will one day save France.
suggested_refs: The essay plate of the tower and the fairy field (media/other/17873794418796089.jpg)
sources: instagram/2022-12-22-joffrey-bourlemont-nacio-en-medio-de.md ('un portal de magia celta… un espíritu adolescente que algún día salvaría a Francia')

stops.name: Château de Bourlémont, the death of the seneschal
stops.campa: In the year 1268 Joffrey de Bourlémont dies in his rebuilt castle, an old crusader of fifty-seven, Sibylle's husband, the king's seneschal, the children's dragon-keeper. The lordship passes on; the charter sleeps at Mureau; the well keeps its water and the tower its view. Of his long errand the valley keeps what valleys keep: three stones, one story, and a tree that has learned the names of things it intends to remember for two hundred years, until a scribe and a spinner of light are born to receive them.
suggested_refs: Georges Poull, Les sires de Bourlémont, 1149-1412 (vol. I)

stops.name: Neufchâteau: Lois de Conte, two hundred years after
stops.campa: Lois de Conte is born at Neufchâteau on the sixth of January, two hundred years after Joffrey, on his very feast of the Kings. Sent to Domremy after a raid of Burgundian bandits, he is taught his letters by the priest Guillaume Fronte and becomes the scribe of the Children of the Tree: the same dance, the same beech, the same well and tower. Among the five children of Jacques and Isabelle he grows closest to Joan, who shares his birthday. The legacy has found its clerk, and the clerk has found his subject.
suggested_refs: Mark Twain, Personal Recollections of Joan of Arc, the Sieur Louis de Conte

stops.name: The tree, Joan's garlands at the well
stops.campa: Joan sings and dances with the children around the old beech, weaves garlands of flowers and herbs and leaves them for the fairies on the boughs and at Joffrey's spring. Her godmother has told her the romance of the tree: that in old times a lord of Bourlémont met a lady called Fée beneath it and they talked together. She drinks from the well the old crusader built for children he did not yet know. The tree that heard the dragons and the Rock beneath the Dome begins, very quietly, to answer.
suggested_refs: Joan's testimony on the Fairy Tree, trial of condemnation, 24 February 1431
sources: joan_of_arc.journey.json, the Tree of Bourlemont stop (same pin)

stops.name: The tower, Saint Barbara and the black window
stops.campa: The tower stands locked now, but Joan claims access by night. Within it she communes with Saint Barbara, the maiden of the tower, who teaches her the science of artillery and how to open portals. She tells Lois of her hair standing on end, of a black window opening in the wall framed by brilliant lightning, of being one and the same with Barbara and with all the maidens of the tower who are spinning thread of light. Joffrey's stone chair of grief has become an engine of annunciation, exactly as the field intended.
suggested_refs: Saint Barbara with her tower, patroness of artillery, the maiden of the black window
sources: instagram/2022-12-26-lois-de-conte-nacio-el-6.md ('la doncella de la torre… la ciencia de la artillería y cómo abrir portales')

stops.name: The tree, the testimony of the fairy
stops.campa: At the Rehabilitation inquiry, before the notaries at Domremy, Joan's godmother, Jeanne, widow of Thiesselin de Vittel, testifies to the romance she once told the child: that in ancient times the lord Pierre de Bourlément and a lady named Fée met beneath this tree and conversed together. The family's name and the fairy enter the parchment record wed under the boughs. The well gives water; the children still dance; and the fire Joffrey carried home from Greccio and Jerusalem has done exactly what he told them it would.
suggested_refs: Deposition of Jeanne, widow of Thiesselin de Vittel, Domrémy inquiry, 1456 (Quicherat, Procès, t. II)
